item.title: Incarico post-doc: Clinical-biological characterization and study of prognostic and predictive factors of response in myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemias. (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 12:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-09 Malattie del sangue, oncologia e reumatologia

The research program aims to study and characterize clinically and molecularly myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemias through the use of advanced sequencing technologies and the integration of clinical, hematological, cytogenetic, and molecular data. The goal is to identify new biomarkers and prognostic and predictive factors for treatment response, further exploring the relationships between molecular profiling, clinical course, and disease progression. Particular attention will be paid to the study of clonal evolution and molecular dynamics associated with disease progression and treatment response, in order to gain a deeper understanding of the biological mechanisms…

item.title: Incarico post-doc: REVIVE-CAP - Risk-guidEd preVentIon of long-term cardioVascular sEquelae after Community-Acquired Pneumonia (GA n. 101344053) (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-10 Gastroenterologia, malattie infettive e malattie cutanee

The REVIVE-CAP project will last 4 years and aims to improve the prevention, diagnosis and management of long-term cardiovascular sequelae following community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). The research activities will include the characterization of post-CAP cardiovascular sequelae across different European countries; the early identification of high- risk patients; the development and validation of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based tool for cardiovascular risk prediction

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Investigating the role of NEUral driven PlGF-NRP1 axis in shaping the vascular niche of recruited and self-renewing arterial MACrophages during aortic aneurysm (Finanziato dal Fondo Italiano per la Scienza FIS3 (FIS-2024-06736) CUP B53C25003640001 (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-04 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Latina
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-26 Scienze tecn. di medicina di labor., sc. delle prof. sanit. tecn. diagnostiche, assist. e della prevenzione, sc. delle prof. sanit. della riabilitazione, sc. tecn. med. e chirurg. avanzate

Aortic aneurysms are focal dilatations of the artery wall. Nervous and immune systems, in particular arterial macrophages, are crucial players in modulating vascular contractility. The aim of this research is to understand how nervous and immune systems interact during aortic aneurism progression and how they affect vascular function, in order to modulate immune response and counteract aortic aneurysm progression. The candidate role will be to investigate functional interactions established between neurons, immune cells and the vasculature in aorta developing aneurysm.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Identification of MAML1-induced molecular mechanisms underlying chemoresistance processes (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-23 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-02 Patologia generale e patologia clinica

Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive tumor subtype, characterized by early onset, high metastatic capacity, and a high recurrence rate, representing a significant clinical challenge. Currently, platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors (indicated in tumors with BRCA1/2 gene mutations) are the mainstay of systemic treatment aimed at inducing DNA damage and replicative stress. However, a significant proportion of patients show primary or acquired resistance to such treatments. In this context, the MAML1 protein emerges as a potential key regulator of tumor progression. item.title: Incarico post-doc: The Role of Antiphospholipid Antibodies in NETosis (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-04 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-09 Malattie del sangue, oncologia e reumatologia

The present project aims to investigate the role of antiphospholipid antibodies, particularly anti-β2GPI antibodies, in promoting NET formation and modulating endothelial cell activation, with particular attention to the mechanisms linking innate immunity, inflammation, and thrombosis. The research will focus on evaluating the ability of anti-β2GPI antibodies to induce NETosis and characterizing the effects of antibody-induced NETs on endothelial cells. Particular attention will be paid to the expression of adhesion molecules, including intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), as well as tissue factor (TF), a key mediator of coagulation…

item.description:

Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-26 Scienze tecn. di medicina di labor., sc. delle prof. sanit. tecn. diagnostiche, assist. e della prevenzione, sc. delle prof. sanit. della riabilitazione, sc. tecn. med. e chirurg. avanzate

Testicular tumors are a heterogeneous group of neoplasms for which currently available biomarkers still show limited accuracy and sensitivity. Some miRNAs have demonstrated significant diagnostic potential in testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs); however, data on their expression profiles in serum and seminal plasma from patients with seminoma and non-germ cell tumors, such as Leydig cell tumors, are lacking. The first aim of this study is therefore to characterize the profile of small non-coding RNAs (miRNAs and piRNAs) in malignant and benign testicular tumors. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Identification of post-transcriptional modifications of tumor suppressors in tumorigenic processes and their role in modulating the expression of immune checkpoints (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-17 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-02 Patologia generale e patologia clinica

Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) frequently harbors mutations in tumor suppressor genes—including *TP53*—that are associated with tumor progression and treatment resistance. Mutant p53 (mutp53) has been shown to sustain HDAC6 expression, thereby promoting DNA damage repair and resistance to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress via ATF6. Preliminary data suggest that ATF6 increases TRAPPC4 expression, promoting the trafficking of PD-L1 to the cell membrane. Furthermore, HDAC6 deacetylates MSH2 and promotes its degradation, thereby impairing mismatch repair and contributing to mutation accumulation, neoantigen production, and immune checkpoint expression.
